title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Termly Exam #18 (Term 3)

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What happens when you push a book gently with a finger compared with a hard push? (1 mark)
   A. It flies away with the gentle push
   B. It moves faster with the gentle push
   C. It moves slowly with the gentle push
   D. It does not move with the hard push

2. Which of these is a problem caused by friction? (1 mark)
   A. Lighting a match
   B. Braking a bicycle
   C. Wearing away of shoes and tyres
   D. Walking safely

3. Which of these is a use of friction? (1 mark)
   A. Wasting energy
   B. Brakes stopping a bicycle
   C. Making parts hot
   D. Machines wearing out

4. Which of these needs friction to work? (1 mark)
   A. Walking on the ground
   B. Skating on wet ice
   C. A rolling wheel
   D. Sliding on oil

5. A cyclist pedals harder and goes faster. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Changes shape
   B. Decreases speed
   C. Stops motion
   D. Increases speed

6. A hockey stick hits a rolling ball to the left. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Starts motion
   B. Changes direction
   C. Changes shape only
   D. Holds together

7. How can a farmer keep a wheelbarrow running smoothly? (1 mark)
   A. Add sand to the wheel
   B. Leave it in the rain
   C. Oil its moving joints
   D. Use rough paint

8. What direction does friction act in compared with the motion of an object? (1 mark)
   A. Sideways only
   B. The same
   C. Upwards only
   D. Opposite

9. What does a green traffic light tell a driver? (1 mark)
   A. Sleep
   B. Stop at once
   C. Stop
   D. Go

10. What is the purpose of skylights? (1 mark)
   A. Block light
   B. Make the house hot
   C. Let rain in on purpose
   D. Let daylight through the roof

11. Which of these is a natural source of light? (1 mark)
   A. A torch
   B. The sun
   C. A candle
   D. A bulb

12. What do solar panels change sunlight into? (1 mark)
   A. Food
   B. Sound
   C. Water
   D. Electricity

13. What does a red traffic light tell a driver? (1 mark)
   A. Go
   B. Stop
   C. Speed up
   D. Turn on lights

14. What does a translucent roof sheet do? (1 mark)
   A. Blocks all light
   B. Makes light
   C. Creates sound
   D. Lets some light in

15. Which of these gives out heat when rubbed? (1 mark)
   A. Hands
   B. A leaf
   C. A book in a bag
   D. A stone table

16. Heat always moves from (1 mark)
   A. A hotter place to a cooler place
   B. A dark place to a bright place
   C. A wet place to a dry place
   D. A cooler place to a hotter place

17. Which of these uses electricity to make heat? (1 mark)
   A. Bicycle
   B. Electric kettle
   C. Wooden chair
   D. Book

18. Which of these sources of heat uses electricity? (1 mark)
   A. Firewood
   B. Electric iron
   C. The sun
   D. Charcoal jiko

19. Why should pupils not touch hot sufurias? (1 mark)
   A. They make sound
   B. They can burn their skin
   C. They become bigger
   D. They become cold

20. What is heat? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of sound
   B. A type of gas
   C. A kind of matter
   D. A form of energy that makes things hot

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Classify these as natural or artificial: candle, stars, torch, lightning, firefly, solar lamp. (4 marks)

22. Explain why we should reduce friction in machines and how it can be done. (5 marks)

23. Explain why light is important in our daily lives. (5 marks)

24. Describe how to investigate the effect of different surfaces on friction using a ramp and a block. Include what you keep the same. (5 marks)

25. Describe four effects of forces using examples from daily life. (4 marks)

26. Why do we use kitchen gloves when holding hot pots? (2 marks)

27. Give two effects of force on objects. (2 marks)

28. Explain why a mirror or a shiny cup is not a source of light. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — It moves slowly with the gentle push
   A bigger force gives a bigger effect.

2. C — Wearing away of shoes and tyres
   Friction wears surfaces away.

3. B — Brakes stopping a bicycle
   Brakes use friction to slow wheels.

4. A — Walking on the ground
   Walking needs grip from friction.

5. D — Increases speed
   More force increases speed.

6. B — Changes direction
   The direction of the ball changes.

7. C — Oil its moving joints
   Oil reduces friction.

8. D — Opposite
   Friction acts against motion.

9. D — Go
   Green means go.

10. D — Let daylight through the roof
   Skylights are roof openings or sheets that let light in.

11. B — The sun
   The sun is found in nature.

12. D — Electricity
   Solar panels make electricity from sunlight.

13. B — Stop
   Red means stop.

14. D — Lets some light in
   It lets daylight in but you cannot see through it clearly.

15. A — Hands
   Rubbing produces heat through friction.

16. A — A hotter place to a cooler place
   Heat moves from hot to cold.

17. B — Electric kettle
   A kettle is heated by electricity.

18. B — Electric iron
   An electric iron uses electricity.

19. B — They can burn their skin
   Hot metal burns.

20. D — A form of energy that makes things hot
   Heat is a form of energy.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Natural: stars, lightning, firefly. Artificial: candle, torch, solar lamp.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair, plus 1 mark for correct table.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Friction wears out parts, wastes energy and makes machines hot. It is reduced by oiling, smoothing, using rollers or ball bearings.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for methods.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: It lets us see, keeps us safe, helps plants to make food, dries clothes, gives solar power and discourages pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a ramp. Slide a block down it covered with cloth, paper, cardboard and bare board. Measure how far it slides each time. Keep the same block, same ramp height and same push. Record in a table. The shortest distance shows the most friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for ramp, 1 mark for surfaces, 1 mark for measuring, 1 mark for fair test, 1 mark for conclusion.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: A force changes the shape of dough, starts a ball moving, stops a bicycle with brakes and changes the direction of a ball when hit with a stick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each effect with an example.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gloves are poor passers of heat so they protect hands from burns.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for poor at passing heat and 1 mark for protection from burns.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Change shape, start motion, stop motion, increase speed, decrease speed, change direction, hold things together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: It does not make its own light. It only reflects light that falls on it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for not making light, 1 mark for reflecting, 1 mark for explanation.
